primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
primary_antecedent.scope: Independent complete trapping/escape equivalence with the stationary convention explicit, principal-type definition and exact receiving audit of Section 26.11. It is not an assertion that a stationary singleton is a regular nonzero-tangent curve.

source_correspondence: The equivalence is stated with stationary characteristic singletons explicit. On the regular characteristic locus the two regular trapping alternatives agree with the source. The multiple-characteristic example explains why nonzero-tangent curves alone cannot detect stationary points.
Necessity treats dp=0, full persistent rank-one characteristics and entire rank-two leaves separately. The actual regular semibicharacteristic definition and characteristic saturation are retained.

Positive homogeneous normalization preserves characteristic directions. Compact metric/unit-tangent data give uniform bounds, while a radial projected zero is a complete characteristic ray in the persistent set and is explicitly excluded.

The phase is the exact algebraic function of point and oriented unit tangent. Its full Hamilton lift is real, and the radial logarithmic ODE has bounded coefficient. No arbitrary continuous argument or completeness of an arbitrarily slowed parameter is assumed.

A trapped half-curve is translated with both point and tangent retained. Fixed signed real local fields, finite-chart continuous dependence, a common positive flow-time bound and finite derivative upper bounds produce an actual two-sided complete limit.
Finite-length accessing arcs and flow uniqueness exclude saturation and N11 from that complete limit. The full lifted curve lies in the persistent set, contradicting the exact trapping condition.

Both branches outside saturation terminate at valid endpoints. In a saturated leaf the missing inactive side cannot remain trapped. Multiplier gluing keeps a strict nonzero real coefficient on every common rank-one germ.

The active part of each leaf is connected by a positive-face component assignment. The proof handles one-sided inactive intervals and infinitely many zeros; it does not assume finitely many positive components.

Whole-fiber quotient overlaps contain rank-two collars. Actual vertical passages and collar connectors give finite corridors. Last-intersection separation and parallel real-flow passages remove overlaps; a reserved quotient disk protects the marked passage from being trimmed away.

A finite real-flow band has one common injective width. A smooth flat-angle turn inside its starting rank-two collar joins two admissible sides, retaining the marked point and producing two endpoints in the outside rank-two target.

The outside cap preserves the coisotropic leaf and old active component. The active and inactive marked cases are both treated. First-contact truncation uses the exact vanishing boundary first jet to return to the original symbol.

The principal-type definition is applied to properly supported scalar classical operators on every compact set. The exact completed gain and semi-global existence proofs are reused with all real orders, strict finite Sobolev targets, the actual obstruction and one smooth solution.

Three complete solutions cover the stationary counterexample, an actual rotating homogeneous symbol and a flat-angle turn with every straight endpoint jet. Forty-five exact finite checks establish only their stated normalization and turn identities.

stationary_characteristic_convention: Regular one-dimensional characteristics require nonzero tangent; Ncrit stationary singletons are explicit additional obstructions. Equivalently, include those singletons in the complete-obstruction convention. No stationary regular curve is invented.
component_scope: The compact-support existence theorem uses a two-ended escape arc through every characteristic point. We now relate that condition to complete characteristic curves and two-dimensional leaves. The compactness argument retains an oriented tangent as well as a point. The rank-two argument retains actual real Hamilton curves rather than assuming that an arbitrary path in a collapsed quotient has a regular lift.
